Enhancer site annotations from the FANTOM5 project and gene annotations from Ensembl were used to obtain raw expression counts for eRNAs and protein-coding genes. Differential expression and co-expression analyses were performed to identify eRNAs associated with AML and their potential co-expressed genes. Functional enrichment analysis was used to determine biological pathways associated with the co-expressed genes of eRNAs. Two eRNAs associated with AML-related pathways were selected for experimental validation using real-time PCR. Two eRNAs, designated eRNA-7A (chr7:157299821-157300521, (hg38)) and eRNA-22A (chr22:29199767-29199953, (hg38)), were significantly upregulated in AML samples compared with normal controls. Real-time PCR confirmed their elevated expression levels in AML patients. Co-expression and functional enrichment analyses identified genes and pathways associated with these eRNAs, showing that genes positively correlated with eRNA-7A and eRNA-22A were significantly enriched in the Myc targets v1 and v2 pathways. Notably, several enriched genes in these pathways have been previously linked to AML pathogenesis. The eRNAs identified in this study, along with their associated genes and pathways, provide a preliminary understanding of the molecular mechanisms underlying AML development and progression. Moreover, they suggest the existence of promising candidates for future biomarker development in AML.

title: Ribosomal RNA-derived fragments in cancer: molecular identity, cellular context, and functional evidence.
abstract: Ribosomal RNA-derived fragments (rRFs), also termed rRNA-derived small RNAs (rsRNAs), occur in cells and biofluids, but their detection does not establish biological activity. This review systematically summarizes current research on rRF biogenesis, intracellular functions, extracellular localization and carriage, and clinical associations, while emphasizing that the detection of rRFs does not in itself establish biological function. Stress-associated cleavage, candidate-specific non-canonical processing, and extracellular ribosome fragmentation can each contribute to the observed repertoire. Functional cancer studies remain concentrated in a few candidates: depletion of a 28S-derived rRF3 affects H1299 cell phenotypes; rsRNA-28S inhibition increases PTGIS expression and taxane resistance in prostate-cancer cells; and synthetic gastric-cancer S2 and S7 mimics alter target reporters and protein abundance. These findings do not establish a common rRF pathway or therapeutic efficacy. Tissue and circulating signatures show diagnostic or prognostic associations, including a methylation-sensitive 28S fragment assay, but many cohorts are small and lack prospective external validation. Therapeutic development could test inhibition of a confirmed tumor-promoting fragment or replacement of a protective fragment, provided that endogenous function, selectivity over parental rRNA, delivery, and safety are established. Overall, rRFs show emerging biological and biomarker potential in cancer, but their clinical translation will require stronger mechanistic validation, prospective clinical evidence, and rigorous assessment of delivery and safety.

title: Persistent Malignant Stem Cells Drive Relapse After Transplantation in the Myelodysplastic Neoplasms.
abstract: The myelodysplastic neoplasms (MDS) are initiated in hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs). Allogeneic transplantation is the only curative treatment, but relapse remains common. To detect rare MDS HSCs, we developed an ultra-low-input DNA sequencing assay and applied it to a multicenter post-transplant cohort. HSC mutation detection preceded relapse by a mean of 98 days and strongly predicted relapse (95.7% vs. 30.3%; hazard ratio, 8.8; P=1.5e-7). Mutations detected only in unfractionated marrow did not predict relapse. We developed methods to measure donor-host HSC chimerism, improving relapse prediction sensitivity. Single-cell protein, DNA, and RNA analyses with mitochondrial lineage tracing confirmed MDS cell enrichment within immunophenotypically- and transcriptionally-defined HSCs, identifying shared ribosomal gene downregulation and candidate mechanisms of venetoclax sensitivity. Venetoclax/azacytidine depleted detectable MDS HSCs in longitudinally evaluated patients. These findings establish that HSC mutation detection predicts post-transplant relapse, provide a rationale for preemptive intervention, and define shared biological features of transplant-resistant MDS HSCs.

title: Multiomics Analysis of Malignant Pleural Mesothelioma Reveals the Immunological Microenvironment Associated with MTAP Loss and Immunotherapy Outcomes.
abstract: Nivolumab plus ipilimumab is a standard first-line therapy for unresectable malignant pleural mesothelioma (MPM), yet biomarkers predicting immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) efficacy remain undefined. We aimed to identify genomic and tumor immune microenvironmental features associated with ICI response in MPM. We analyzed two independent MPM cohorts. The discovery cohort included patients at the National Cancer Center Hospital (2012-2022) with frozen tumor tissues available for whole-genome sequencing (WGS) and RNA sequencing. Genomic alterations, transcriptomic profiles, immune cell composition, and T-cell receptor repertoire were analyzed, and key findings were validated in a nationwide Center for Cancer Genomics and Advanced Therapeutics (C-CAT) cohort. The WGS cohort comprised 52 patients. Among ICI-treated patients, overall response rates were 30% in the WGS cohort and 29.4% in the C-CAT cohort. Genomic analyses identified frequent alterations in BAP1 and NF2, across both cohorts. ICI responders showed higher T-cell receptor diversity, increased CD8⁺ T-cell infiltration, and enrichment of M1 macrophages compared with non-responders. MTAP loss was associated with higher CD8⁺ T-cell infiltration and T-cell receptor diversity, and was linked to a higher ICI response rate in the C-CAT cohort. In contrast, BAP1 and NF2 alterations showed no consistent association with immune features or ICI efficacy. An immune-active tumor microenvironment characterized by high T-cell receptor diversity, CD8⁺ T-cell infiltration, and M1 macrophage enrichment was associated with favorable ICI responses in MPM. MTAP loss was linked to immune-related features and a higher ICI response, supporting further investigation of MTAP loss as a candidate biomarker.

title: Single-cell Bioinformatics Analysis and In Vitro Validation Explore Core Genes and Signaling Pathways of Iron Metabolism in Fetal Left Heart Function Injury in Gestational Diabetes Mellitus.
abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is a common metabolic disorder during pregnancy that significantly affects fetal cardiac development. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying iron metabolism-related pathways in GDM-induced fetal left heart dysfunction remain incompletely understood. This study employed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) technology combined with bioinformatics analysis and published echocardiographic data validation to comprehensively characterize the cellular landscape and iron metabolism signatures in publicly available GDM fetal cardiac transcriptomic data from the GEO database (GSM5261695 and GSM5261697). Analysis of 4,531 cells identified 17 distinct clusters comprising 9 major cardiac cell types. Cardiomyocytes exhibited the highest iron metabolism dysregulation scores. Ferroptosis pathway analysis revealed elevated GPX4 and SLC7A11 expression with concurrent ACSL4 downregulation in GDM samples. Clinical ultrasound validation demonstrated significant left ventricular dysfunction in GDM fetuses, including reduced ejection fraction and impaired diastolic function. RT-qPCR validation confirmed significant upregulation of GPX4 (2.45-fold), SLC7A11 (2.87-fold), and FTH1 (2.31-fold) in high glucose-treated cardiomyocytes, with concurrent ACSL4 downregulation (0.52-fold). GPX4 protein validation by immunofluorescence and Western blot further showed higher GPX4 signal in the OGD group and reduced GPX4 expression after GPX4 knockdown. This study reveals that dysregulated iron metabolism and ferroptosis resistance in fetal cardiomyocytes serve as critical mechanisms underlying GDM-induced left heart dysfunction. The identification of cell type-specific iron metabolism signatures provides novel therapeutic targets for preventing and treating fetal cardiac complications in GDM pregnancies.

title: Exploring the role of RPS2 in muscle-invasive bladder cancer progression and resistance: A nanovesicle-based therapeutic approach.
abstract: Chemotherapy resistance in muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) remains a major clinical challenge, and the role of ribosomal protein S2 (RPS2) has not been fully clarified. This study investigated the mechanistic association between RPS2 and MIBC progression and developed an asparagine-glycine-arginine (NGR)-modified nanovesicle system for targeted RPS2 modulation to reverse chemotherapy resistance. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) identified distinct tumor subpopulations, and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) revealed gene modules associated with stemness. Differential expression analysis of patients treated with cisplatin highlighted key genes linked to stemness and resistance. In vitro experiments showed that RPS2 inhibition suppressed proliferation and invasion while enhancing cisplatin sensitivity in MIBC cells. The engineered NGR-modified red blood cell (RBC) membrane vesicles (RMVs) encapsulating RPS2 small interfering RNA (siRNA) (NGR-RMVs@si-RPS2) vesicles effectively targeted tumor vasculature, inhibited xenograft growth, and restored cisplatin sensitivity in resistant tumors, demonstrating strong therapeutic potential. These findings establish RPS2 as a critical regulator of MIBC chemoresistance and present NGR-modified nanovesicles as a promising strategy for improving treatment outcomes.

title: SLC5A12 defines an invasive epithelial state associated with immune remodeling and therapeutic vulnerability in HNSCC.
abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is characterized by marked epithelial and immune heterogeneity. The malignant epithelial states associated with tumor progression, immune remodeling, and potential therapeutic vulnerability remain incompletely defined. Single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets from three HNSCC cohorts were integrated with TCGA-HNSC and five GEO cohorts. Epithelial-state heterogeneity, inferred trajectories, regulons, cell-cell communication, prognostic features, spatial localization, and ferroptosis-associated transcriptional programs were analyzed. SLC5A12 was prioritized through convergent computational analyses and was subsequently tested by loss-of-function assays and xenograft experiments. CellOracle perturbation, ferroptosis-related drug-sensitivity analyses, and molecular docking were treated as computational predictions. Five epithelial states were identified, among which the Invasive population increased with disease progression and exhibited the highest inferred CNV burden. Invasive cells showed enrichment of malignant and extracellular-matrix programs and prominent predicted MIF-CD74/CXCR4 communication with regulatory T cells. Machine-learning, WGCNA, single-cell, and spatial analyses converged on SLC5A12 as an Invasive-state-associated prognostic feature. Computational analyses further indicated a ferroptosis-associated vulnerability profile in the Invasive state and predicted attenuation of invasive and immunoregulatory programs after virtual SLC5A12 loss. Experimentally, SLC5A12 knockdown reduced proliferation, clonogenicity, migration, invasion, and xenograft growth while increasing apoptosis. Structure-based virtual screening nominated ledipasvir (ZINC000150338819) and elbasvir (ZINC000150588351) as top-ranked candidate SLC5A12-binding compounds. SLC5A12 is a molecular feature of an Invasive epithelial state associated with HNSCC progression, adverse outcome, and predicted immune-remodeling and therapeutic-vulnerability programs. Experimental loss-of-function data support a tumor-promoting role for SLC5A12, whereas the MIF-Treg communication, ferroptosis vulnerability, CellOracle perturbation, and molecular-docking findings remain computational hypotheses requiring direct validation.

title: Sex-based differences in fibrosis markers in human abdominal aortic aneurysms.
abstract: Abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAA) are a complex degenerative vascular disease. The role of fibrosis in AAA progression is unclear. Our study evaluated the impact of fibroblast activation protein (FAP), collagen, and vimentin on AAA fibrosis and progression. We hypothesized that FAP may influence fibrosis and disease severity in AAA, with potential sex-specific differences. Multi-centered transcriptomic analysis of aortic samples from 15 human AAA and 5 non-AAA was performed to evaluate cell-specific fibrosis gene expression profiles. Histopathological and molecular analysis of 26 male and female AAA samples (mAAA and fAAA) and 29 male and female normal abdominal aortas (mNAA and fNAA) was performed to assess whole-tissue fibrosis markers and signaling. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) analysis identified eight major cell clusters with distinct sex-based distributions. Although vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) and fibroblast clusters had reduced counts in both male and female AAAs, they more highly expressed FAP and COL1A1 genes, particularly in females. Whole-tissue analysis demonstrated elevated extracellular matrix deposits with markedly increased collagen type 1 in both mAAA and fAAA. Alpha-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA)-positive VSMCs were also reduced in mAAA and fAAA, but FAP was notably elevated, and robustly in fAAA. FAP-positive fibroblasts in fAAA exhibited increased expression of fibrosis markers, suggesting a unique pro-fibrotic phenotype. Our study reveals a sex-based difference in AAA tissue, with elevated fibrosis markers and increased FAP levels in females, suggesting its significant role in disease progression. These findings underscore the potential of FAP as a unique tissue biomarker for AAAs and warrants further investigation into novel targeted therapies that aim to stabilize AAAs, particularly in female patients.

title: Reanalysis of public bulk and single-nucleus transcriptomes identifies widespread tumor-normal dysregulation and a cross-layer cell-cycle signal in sinonasal squamous cell carcinoma.
abstract: Sinonasal squamous cell carcinoma (SNSCC) is a rare malignancy affecting the nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses, with human papillomavirus (HPV) infection identified as a critical etiological factor in a subset of cases. HPV-positive and HPV-negative SNSCC exhibit distinct clinical behaviors, with HPV-positive tumors generally demonstrating better prognosis and treatment response. However, the cellular composition and transcriptomic landscape of SNSCC tumor versus normal tissue remain incompletely characterized. Multi-layer transcriptomic reanalysis of publicly available single-nucleus and bulk RNA sequencing data provides an opportunity to systematically identify tumor-normal gene expression changes and nominate candidate biomarkers for prospective validation. We reanalyzed publicly available single-nucleus RNA sequencing data (GSE277797: one healthy nasal mucosa library, HC1; one SNSCC tumor library, CA5) together with bulk RNA-seq data from 14 SNSCC and normal nasal mucosa samples (GSE278145), microarray data from five matched tumor-adjacent-normal pairs (GSE138809), and a 21-sample sinonasal cancer tumor-only context cohort (GSE118386). Following rigorous quality control, doublet detection, cell-type annotation using canonical markers, and program scoring, we integrated findings across data layers. Candidate genes were further assessed by in vitro experiments in two SNSCC cell lines (RPMI 2650 and Detroit 562) compared with normal bronchial epithelial BEAS-2B cells, using quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) to evaluate mRNA expression levels (2-ΔΔCT method, GAPDH reference) and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) to quantify secreted and intracellular protein concentrations. Single-nucleus analysis resolved 14,479 nuclei into 11 biological cell types, with the largest observed compositional shift being an increase in Epithelial cells (+44.7 percentage points) and a decrease in Secretory epithelial cells (-56.2 percentage points) in the tumor library relative to the healthy library. Bulk RNA-seq differential expression testing across 17,677 genes identified 5,732 genes at FDR <0.05, with cell-cycle genes showing the largest program-level shift (+1.727 standardized units). Cross-layer integration yielded a Spearman correlation of 0.543 between bulk fold-changes and single-nucleus pseudobulk shifts. Candidate genes including CD74, CCL5, IL32, and HLA-DRA showed concordant upregulation across data layers. In vitro qRT-PCR confirmed significant mRNA upregulation of CD74 (4.27-fold), CCL5 (3.15-fold), IL32 (3.68-fold), and HLA-DRA (3.82-fold) in RPMI 2650 cells compared to normal BEAS-2B cells (all p < 0.01), with elevated protein levels further corroborated by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. This multi-layer transcriptomic reanalysis of publicly available SNSCC datasets identifies consistent tumor-versus-normal dysregulation across single-nucleus and bulk platforms, and nominates CD74, CCL5, IL32, and HLA-DRA as candidate biomarkers warranting prospective clinical validation. These findings are exploratory and should be interpreted within the constraints of the available single-sample single-nucleus data.

title: Keratin 17 Defines an Epithelial-Mesenchymal Transition-Associated Migratory Cell State in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma.
abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is characterized by early invasion, metastasis, and therapeutic resistance that contribute substantially to its poor clinical outcome. Keratin 17 (K17) is a recognized marker of the aggressive basal-like subtype of PDAC and an independent predictor of adverse prognosis; however, the biological basis for this association remains incompletely understood. To define K17-associated cellular programs, we integrated single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data from 42 patients, Clinical Proteomic Tumor Analysis Consortium (CPTAC) proteomic data from 140 tumors, MACSima multiplex spatial imaging of 63 patients, dual-plex immunohistochemistry of 60 cases, and three-dimensional spheroid migration assays. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis demonstrated significant enrichment of epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT)-associated gene programs among K17-positive malignant epithelial cells. Consistent with this finding, K17-positive tumors in the CPTAC cohort exhibited enrichment of the Hallmark EMT pathway at the protein level. Among six candidate markers identified through transcriptomic analyses, laminin subunit gamma-2 (LAMC2) was the only candidate associated with K17 at every validation step. Tumors positive for both K17 and LAMC2 had significantly worse overall survival than double-negative tumors (adjusted hazard ratio = 2.53). Multiplex spatial imaging localized K17-positive cells predominantly to poorly differentiated tumor regions and demonstrated frequent single-cell co-expression with LAMC2. Whole-slide dual-plex immunohistochemistry further confirmed the association between K17 and LAMC2 and showed progressive enrichment of K17/LAMC2-positive tumor cells with increasing intratumoral histologic grade. Functionally, gain- and loss-of-function studies in three-dimensional PDAC spheroids demonstrated that K17 promotes migratory outgrowth, and differences in proliferation did not account for this effect. Collectively, these findings identify K17 as a marker of a poorly differentiated, EMT-associated migratory cell state in PDAC and provide functional evidence that K17 contributes to tumor-cell migration.
